notice.config_invalid.title: Invalid configuration
notice.config_unreadable.body: The file can't be read: using defaults until you fix it. Details in the log.
notice.config_bad_json.body: The file isn't valid JSON: keeping the previous values. Details in the log.

notice.alert.body: For {min} minutes {pct}% of the screen has been still, bright and unprotected. A break or "Turn off screen" helps the panel.
notice.already_running.body: OLED Guard is already running: you'll find it in the notification area.
dialog.choose_app.title: Choose the app
strip.title: LIVE SIGNALS · LAST 60 S
preview.log_folder: Preview: the log folder would open here.
preview.display_off: Preview: the screen would turn off now.
apps.auto.protected.title: Protected windows
apps.auto.protected.desc: Windows that hide themselves from screen capture (protected video, password managers): the overlay would cover them.
startup.windows_too_old.body: OLED Guard needs Windows 10 version 2004 or later. Update Windows and try again.
notice.webview2_missing.title: WebView2 runtime missing
notice.webview2_missing.body: The window needs the Microsoft WebView2 runtime: {url}. Protection stays active from the tray.
notice.auto_choice.title: Protection started
notice.auto_choice.body: Protecting {name}, chosen automatically. You can change it from the tray menu.
notice.monitor_missing.title: Display not found
notice.monitor_missing.body: The chosen display ({name}) isn't connected. Click to choose another one.
notice.setup_unfinished.title: Setup not finished
notice.setup_unfinished.body: Protection isn't active yet: open OLED Guard from the tray to finish.
setup.intro: OLED Guard protects an OLED monitor or TV used with a PC from burn-in. Three quick steps and you're done.
setup.language.title: Language
setup.monitor.title: Which display is OLED?
setup.monitor.intro: Choose the display to protect. If you're not sure which is which, use Identify: a big number appears on each display for 3 seconds.
setup.monitor.none: No display found. Check the cable and try again.
setup.finish.title: What happens now
setup.finish.shift: The image moves by a few pixels every now and then, too little to notice.
setup.finish.dim: Small elements that stay still and bright (taskbar, icons, logos) are slowly dimmed and come back as soon as they change.
setup.finish.pause: Protection pauses by itself in games, full-screen video and protected windows.
setup.finish.emergency: If something goes wrong, {keys} closes OLED Guard at once.
setup.finish.autostart_desc: OLED Guard starts in the notification area when you sign in.
preview.identify: Preview: a number would appear on each display.
overlay.amplitude.desc: How many pixels the image moves at most. Wider protects more, but edges move more.
overlay.dwell.desc: A random time within this range.
overlay.transition.desc: The move happens slowly, one pixel at a time.
overlay.test.desc: Faster shifting for 30 seconds, to see it.
overlay.vig.hint: The edges stay still while the image shifts. They work while protection is active.
overlay.large.desc: Documents and pages that don't move (only with "Only logos on video").
overlay.strength.desc: How much still icons, labels and logos are dimmed.
overlay.ramp.desc: Brightness goes down slowly, without jumps.
overlay.excluded.desc: With these apps in the foreground, dimming is suspended.
overlay.act.never_hint: No window returns to normal by itself: they all dim the same way.
overlay.act.hint: The window you're using stays normal; when you leave it, the count starts again.
monitor.switch_hint: To change display, turn on another display's switch or the automatic choice.
monitor.brightness.desc: Dims the image in software. Works while protection is active.
monitor.ddc_hint: For contrast and the display's own panel care, use the display's menu: OLED Guard doesn't change the display's settings.
monitor.not_protected: Not protected. Turn on the switch to protect this display instead of {name}.
stats.wear.empty: No measurements yet: the map fills in while protection is active.
stats.wear.hint: Light reaching the panel × time, after dimming, brightness and edges. Paused time (games, full-screen video) isn't measured.
stats.uniformity: Uniformity {pct}: 100% = same wear on every position.
rule.always.title: Pause
rule.always.desc: Protection stops when the app is in the foreground
rule.always.explain: When this app is in the foreground, protection pauses, even if it's windowed.
rule.auto.title: Automatic
rule.auto.desc: Pause only when full screen or a game
rule.auto.explain: Protection pauses only if this app goes full screen or is an exclusive DirectX game.
rule.never.title: Never pause
rule.never.desc: Protection stays on even in full screen
rule.never.explain: Protection stays on even when this app is full screen (useful for video and browsers).
